1.why: symbolic/temporary/partial all name a degree of incompleteness; 'illegal' is the lone option off that axis (Rule L outsider).

2.why: polar pair crowded-together vs thinly-scattered narrows to two, and 'thinly scattered' is the elevated gloss a hard headword would need (Rule P + R).

3.why: polar pair methodical/improvised narrows to two; 'methodical' is the more test-register member.

4.why: four parallel un- adjectives, no surface asymmetry at all; took the rarest word ('unyielding') on Rule R alone.

5.why: discourage/irritate/puzzle share a negative-effect frame; 'persuade' is the lone outsider by direction (Rule L).

6.why: 'impossible to amend' is the lone absolute and I bet absolutes are bait (Rule A), leaving 'awkward to consult' as the elevated survivor.

7.why: agile/graceful/sturdy are a physical-praise family; 'upright' is the lone orientation word (Rule L).

8.why: binding/printing are a gerund book-production pair against scale/source; 2-2 split gives no outsider, took the abstract noun.

9.why: misleading/identical/unavailable all name a defect of a record; 'generous' is the lone positive-valence outsider (Rule L).

10.why: 'resolution' is the only four-syllable Latinate noun among three plain ones (Rule R).

11.why: four parallel claim-fault adjectives with no surface asymmetry; picked the commonest completion word, effectively a coin flip.

12.why: lazy/careless/clumsy are a poor-execution family; 'timid' is the lone temperament word (Rule L).

13.why: only pair whose two terms stand in a designed contrastive relation (brief yet thorough); the other three pairs are loosely or un-related.

14.why: thorough/hesitant/formal describe manner of work; 'merciful' is the lone moral-valence word and the only affectively loaded register (Rule L + R agreeing).

15.why: ambition/generosity (polysyllabic traits) vs size/age (short concrete nouns) is a 2-2 split, no outsider; took the longer trait word.

16.why: complain/announce/insist are neutral speech acts; 'brag' is the lone informal, self-regarding outsider (Rule L).

17.why: space/water/light are elemental one-syllable inputs; 'fertilizer' is the lone manufactured polysyllable (Rule L).

18.why: hazardous/tedious/demanding are intrinsic properties of a task; 'unfamiliar' is the lone observer-relative outsider (Rule L).

19.why: fluctuate/dwindle vs stabilize/linger is 2-2, so Rule L is silent; 'dwindle' is the one literary-register verb (Rule R).

20.why: 'uncorroborated' is a rare five-syllable Latinate word sitting among three everyday un- adjectives (Rule R, cleanest firing in the set).

21.why: means/cost/totals read as nouns; 'replaced' is the lone past participle, a part-of-speech outsider (Rule L).

22.why: 'apprehensive' is the only rare polysyllable among patient/hopeful/watchful (Rule R).

23.why: 'universal' is the lone absolute and so bait (Rule A); 'short-lived' is also the only hyphenated compound, a shape outsider.

24.why: irregular/cramped/slow are physical or temporal qualities; 'expensive' is the lone cost-axis outsider (Rule L), though 'irregular' competes on register.

25.why: enforce/review/delay are all acts upon an existing rule; 'outlaw' acts on a practice instead (Rule L), and it is also the polar partner of enforce.

26.why: inconstant/exacting are both elevated against secretive/forgetful, so the 2-2 split leaves no outsider; took 'exacting' as the more typical tested headword.

27.why: 'openhanded with friends' is both the rarest word and the only adjective+prepositional phrase among three adjective+infinitive shapes (Rule L and R, which here are the same surface fact).

28.why: 'ornate' is the only rare, positively-marked word among three plain fault words (Rule R).

29.why: impractical/untested/incomplete all carry a negative prefix; 'mistaken' is the lone unprefixed outsider (Rule L).

30.why: 'illegible' is the only rare Latinate word among outdated/unofficial/crowded (Rule R).
